name: Federative Republic of Brazil

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 8,510,420 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 8,358,140 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 212,812,405). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:BRA.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 pp.409-410 as quoted: 374,500 active (excludes 395,000 Military Police/fire brigades paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025: ~360,000 (220,000 Army, 70,000 Navy, 70,000 Air Force), low.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 as quoted: 124,600 reserves. High is an educated allowance for the last few discharged conscript classes (~80-90k a year), recallable but not organized in reserve units.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 374,500 (IISS 2026) minus infantry P roles (7,000 + 40,000). Covers navy and air force (~140,000), armour/artillery crews, engineers, logistics, staff and conscripts in garrison duties.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to large conscript-based Latin American armies: Brazil drafts ~80-90k men a year and keeps a large paper reserve, but has little stored equipment; WWII Brazil mobilized only ~25,000 for Italy. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Armoured and mechanized infantry battalions (M113 tracked, Guarani wheeled) of the armoured/mechanized cavalry and infantry brigades, ~12 battalions x ~550. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: M113 and Guarani APCs, IISS counts only 13 Guaranis with 30 mm as IFVs.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional cadre with one-year conscripts; strong jungle/airmobile schools, little combined-arms war experience (MINUSTAH peacekeeping).

count.note: Educated guess. Jungle (CMA), light, mountain, motorized, parachute and airmobile infantry plus ~10,000 combat marines of the CFN. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: era-typical small arms (IA2), limited night vision.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: jungle brigades and parachute/SOF units are well trained; conscripts dilute line units.

count.note: Brazilian Army article (2023, IISS 2023 p.383 as cited): Leopard 1A5 BR 220 + Leopard 1A1 BE 41 + M60A3 TTS 35 = 296 MBTs. Low allows for 1A1 BE and M60 withdrawal as Centauro II arrives.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: Leopard 1A5 is 1980s technology; IISS rates no Brazilian MBT as modern.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional cadre with one-year conscripts; strong jungle/airmobile schools, little combined-arms war experience (MINUSTAH peacekeeping).

count.note: Brazilian Army article (2023): M113/M577 660 + Guarani ~575 + EE-11 Urutu 46 + EE-9 Cascavel 408 + Guaicurus 32 = 1,721. Guarani deliveries continue (~60/yr) while Cascavel is retired.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: modern Guarani 6x6 but many 1970s M113/Cascavel/Urutu.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional cadre with one-year conscripts; strong jungle/airmobile schools, little combined-arms war experience (MINUSTAH peacekeeping).

count.note: IISS (2023) as quoted in the Brazilian Army article: towed 431 (336 105 mm + 95 155 mm) + 155 mm SP (M109) 169 + MLRS 36 (ASTROS II) = 636; 1,245 mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: ASTROS II is modern, most tubes are 1950s M101/M114.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional cadre with one-year conscripts; strong jungle/airmobile schools, little combined-arms war experience (MINUSTAH peacekeeping).

count.note: Active Brazilian military aircraft list: F-39E/F Gripen 13 (+23 on order) + F-5EM 34 = 47. High adds F-5FM two-seaters (4, trainers) and further Gripen deliveries in 2026.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Gripen E is among the best 4.5-generation fighters, but most of the fleet is upgraded F-5.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional FAB, CRUZEX exercise host.

count.note: A-1M AMX 10 + A-29 Super Tucano 81 + Navy A-4KU Skyhawk 3 = 94. AT-27/AT-29 trainers excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: turboprop COIN aircraft and aging AMX/Skyhawk.

count.note: Air Force: H-36 Caracal 14 + VH-35 2 + H-60 16 + H-50 trainer 19 = 51; Army Aviation: HM-2 4 + HA-1 33 + HM-1 32 + HM-3 7 + HM-4 14 = 90; Navy: SH-16 6 + Lynx Mk21 5 + UH-15 15 + UH-12 17 + UH-35 (H135) 2 = 45. Total 186; no dedicated attack helicopters.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Caracal/Black Hawk modern, many Ecureuil light types.

count.note: Hermes 450 4 + Hermes 900 1 (2 lost) + IAI Heron 2 = 7 Air Force; Navy ScanEagle (Brazilian Navy article) ~6, educated count.

Brazilian Navy article (IISS 2025 p.402 as cited): helicopter carrier Atlantico 1 + Niteroi-class frigates 5 + Greenhalgh (Type 22) 1 = 7; mid adds the first Tamandare-class frigate (launched 2024, entering service 2026). Inhauma and Barroso corvettes counted as minor.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 band minus: escorts are 1970s-80s designs with Exocet/Sea Wolf/Aspide; Tamandare (MEKO A-100) modern.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional navy, regular UNITAS exercises.

count.note: Brazilian Navy article (2025): LPD Bahia 1 + LST Almirante Saboia 1 + corvettes 2 (Inhauma, Barroso) + patrol vessels 44 + minesweepers 3 = 51; LPD Oiapoque (ex-HMS Bulwark) high.
Brazilian Navy article: Tupi-class 1 + Tikuna 1 + Riachuelo-class (Scorpene) 3 = 5; high adds the fourth Riachuelo (Almirante Karam) due 2026. Nuclear Alvaro Alberto not before ~2034.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Scorpene-derived Riachuelo with SM39 Exocet; Type 209 older.

count.note: Army article: 34 Gepard SPAAGs in the armoured brigades (~4 per battery, ~9) plus RBS 70/RBS 70 NG and Igla-S MANPADS batteries (~5). No medium-range SAM.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: well-developed staff college system (ECEME), led MINUSTAH 2004-17; no interstate war since 1945.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5 national conscript army with strong professional units (paratroopers, jungle infantry, marines).

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average; no external threat perception, strong for Amazon/sovereignty defence.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: ASTROS II (AV-TM 300 cruise missile not yet operational), Meteor/IRIS-T on Gripen, Exocet; few precision munitions or loitering munitions.

armor.note: Below anchor 9: Leopard 1A5/M60 without composite armour; Guarani modern; Centauro II only arriving.

ships.note: Anchor 9: Scorpene-type submarines, MEKO A-100 frigates entering service; most escorts 1970s.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: few hardened shelters, no layered air defence.

logistics.note: Anchor 9: KC-390 airlift/tankers, large domestic road network, limited sealift.

communications.note: Anchor 9: SGDC military/civil geostationary satellite, Link-BR2 data link.

isr.note: Anchor 9: E-99 AEW, R-99 SIGINT, SISFRON border sensors, Amazonia-1 satellite.

air.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Gripen E (4.5 generation) partially fielded; F-5EM and AMX legacy.

cyber.note: Anchor 9-10: Army Cyber Defence Command (ComDCiber) established 2016.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 3,411,333,864,642 / population 212,812,405 = 16,030 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 4,261,503,890,871 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 3,411,333,864,642 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/BRA/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.05% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 1.1% (2024), 1.3% (2021); mostly personnel and pensions.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 20.15% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.55 -> 0.95. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/BRA/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 7.63% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 1.57 (mean 2021-2023, range 1.49-1.64). Mid 1 - 0.076/1.57 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 1.49 = 0.93. High: s 1.64 = 0.95. Net exporter: production is about 157% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. World-leading net exporter of soy, beef, chicken, sugar and coffee; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 104,657,408 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 7.149% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 1,496,472. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Iveco Defence Vehicles Sete Lagoas builds the Guarani (~60/yr peacetime). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Army)

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Embraer Gaviao Peixoto final assembly of Gripen E/F (15 of 36 built in Brazil), dependent on Swedish/US subsystems. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Brazilian_military_aircraft)

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Embraer A-29 Super Tucano line (export orders), surge feasible. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Brazilian_military_aircraft)

helicopters.note: Educated guess. Helibras (Airbus) Itajuba assembles H225M and AS350/H125. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Brazilian_military_aircraft)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Tamandare-class frigates at Itajai (4 by 2029). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Navy)

submarines.note: Educated guess. ICN Itaguai builds Riachuelo-class boats. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Navy)

roadKm.note: CIA/CNT figures as quoted: 2,000,000 km total (2023), of which 214,000 km paved and 1,786,000 km unpaved, 17,000 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half the unpaved network (derived midpoint) because much of it is seasonal dirt road; high is the total.

railKm.note: World Bank 32,622 km (2007, high); CIA Factbook 29,850 km (2014, mid), mostly metre-gauge freight lines.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 45 ports, 4 large + 7 medium = 11 (Santos, Rio de Janeiro, Itajai, Rio Grande, Tubarao/Vitoria, Salvador, Recife, Belem...).

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 5,922 thousand DWT under the Brazilian flag (4,210 thousand GT), largely Petrobras/Transpetro tankers and offshore vessels. High is an educated allowance for Brazilian-owned foreign-flag tonnage.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck-based sustainment; Amazon operations depend on river transport and airlift.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (~6 million), mules and donkeys; not from FAO data. Some Army cavalry and Amazon pack use.

nuclearWarheads.note: Brazil is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to Tlatelolco and the ABACC safeguards agreement with Argentina; naval nuclear propulsion programme only.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: vast territory and population support; high 1.3 because the Amazon offers deep strategic depth and a climate few invaders are adapted to.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:BRA (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2023-2026 as quoted in the Brazilian Army and Brazilian Navy articles and the personnel list; aircraft from the List of active Brazilian military aircraft (World Air Forces tables). Army vehicle counts are 2023 figures (Guarani deliveries since then raise ifv_apc slightly). ships_major = carriers/LHD + frigates; ships_minor = LPD/LST, corvettes, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). State Military Police (395,000, IISS paramilitary) excluded.
